name: @plexui/vue
description: PlexUI for Vue 3: the same components, props, markup and styles as the React library.

components.name: Accordion
components.description: Vertically stacked panels that expand to reveal content, with one or several items open at a time and full keyboard navigation.

props.name: type
props.description: Required. Whether one item or many can be open at a time

props.name: v-model:value / value
props.description: Controlled open item(s), named like the React prop

props.name: collapsible
props.description: When type="single", allow closing the open item

props.name: @update:value
props.description: Fires when the open item(s) change; closing the open item of a single accordion reports ""

examples.name: Overview
examples.code:
<Accordion type="single" collapsible default-value="shipping" style="width: 100%; max-width: 384px">
  <AccordionItem value="shipping">
    <AccordionTrigger>What are your shipping options?</AccordionTrigger>
    <AccordionContent>
      We offer standard (5–7 business days), express (2–3 days), and
      overnight shipping. Free standard shipping on orders over $50.
    </AccordionContent>
  </AccordionItem>
  <AccordionItem value="returns">
    <AccordionTrigger>What is your return policy?</AccordionTrigger>
    <AccordionContent>
      Returns are accepted within 30 days of delivery. Items must be unused
      and in original packaging. Refunds are processed within 5–7 business
      days of receipt.
    </AccordionContent>
  </AccordionItem>
  <AccordionItem value="support">
    <AccordionTrigger>How can I contact customer support?</AccordionTrigger>
    <AccordionContent>
      Reach us by email, live chat, or phone Monday through Friday, 9am–6pm
      ET. Weekend tickets are handled within 24 hours.
    </AccordionContent>
  </AccordionItem>
</Accordion>

examples.name: Single
examples.code:
<Accordion type="single" collapsible default-value="trial" style="width: 100%; max-width: 384px">
  <AccordionItem
    v-for="item in [
      {
        value: 'trial',
        trigger: 'How long is the free trial?',
        content: '14 days, no credit card required. At the end of the trial you can keep the free tier or upgrade to Pro; your projects stay in place either way.',
      },
      {
        value: 'plan',
        trigger: 'Can I change plans mid-cycle?',
        content: 'Yes. Upgrades are prorated immediately; downgrades take effect at the next billing date. Invoices always reflect the exact span each plan was active.',
      },
      {
        value: 'invoices',
        trigger: 'Where can I find past invoices?',
        content: 'Billing → Invoices in your workspace settings. Every PDF is archived for seven years and can be pulled via the Billing API.',
      },
    ]"
    :key="item.value"
    :value="item.value"
  >
    <AccordionTrigger>{{ item.trigger }}</AccordionTrigger>
    <AccordionContent>{{ item.content }}</AccordionContent>
  </AccordionItem>
</Accordion>
examples.details: Default shape. type="single" + collapsible lets users close the currently open item; without collapsible, one item is always open.

examples.name: Multiple
examples.code:
<Accordion type="multiple" :default-value="['notifications']" style="width: 100%; max-width: 384px">
  <AccordionItem
    v-for="item in [
      {
        value: 'notifications',
        trigger: 'Notification settings',
        content: 'Pick which events trigger email, push, or in-app alerts. Release-blocker incidents always page the on-call regardless of quiet hours.',
      },
      {
        value: 'privacy',
        trigger: 'Privacy & security',
        content: 'Turn on two-factor, review active sessions, and manage connected apps. Workspace admins can also enforce SSO and hardware-key policies org-wide.',
      },
      {
        value: 'billing',
        trigger: 'Billing & subscription',
        content: 'View your current plan, payment method, and upcoming renewal. Seat changes apply immediately; the next invoice will include a prorated adjustment.',
      },
    ]"
    :key="item.value"
    :value="item.value"
  >
    <AccordionTrigger>{{ item.trigger }}</AccordionTrigger>
    <AccordionContent>{{ item.content }}</AccordionContent>
  </AccordionItem>
</Accordion>
examples.details: Use type="multiple" when readers can keep several sections open at once: settings pages, long FAQs, step-by-step references.

examples.name: Disabled
examples.code:
<Accordion type="single" collapsible default-value="history" style="width: 100%; max-width: 384px">
  <AccordionItem value="history">
    <AccordionTrigger>Can I see my usage history?</AccordionTrigger>
    <AccordionContent>
      Yes, the Activity tab logs every API call, deploy, and admin action
      for the last 90 days. Longer retention requires the Enterprise plan.
    </AccordionContent>
  </AccordionItem>
  <AccordionItem value="audit" disabled>
    <AccordionTrigger>Audit log export (Enterprise only)</AccordionTrigger>
    <AccordionContent>
      Upgrade to Enterprise to stream audit events to S3, Splunk, or your
      SIEM of choice.
    </AccordionContent>
  </AccordionItem>
  <AccordionItem value="two-factor">
    <AccordionTrigger>How do I enable two-factor auth?</AccordionTrigger>
    <AccordionContent>
      Settings → Security → Two-factor. You can use an authenticator app or
      a FIDO2 hardware key. Recovery codes are issued once at enrollment.
    </AccordionContent>
  </AccordionItem>
</Accordion>
examples.details: Pass disabled to an AccordionItem to make it read-only. The row stays visible so the reader understands the section exists; keyboard focus skips it.

components.name: Alert
components.description: Inline message for notices and warnings with semantic colors, variants, a title, a description, action slots, and a dismiss control.

props.name: actions-placement
props.description: Placement of actions; automatic from sizing when unset

props.name: actions-class-name
props.description: Class applied to the actions container

props.name: indicator
props.description: Custom indicator (slot), or :indicator="false" to hide it

props.name: @dismiss
props.description: Shows the dismiss button when set

props.name: banner
props.description: Full-width strip: square corners, lines above and below only

examples.name: Overview
examples.code:
<Alert
  title="Scheduled maintenance"
  description="We'll be offline 2 - 4 AM UTC on July 14 while we upgrade our database."
>
  <template #actions>
    <Button color="primary" variant="soft" pill>Dismiss</Button>
  </template>
</Alert>

examples.name: Colors & variants
examples.code: {{ color }}
examples.details: You can stylize the display of the alert using the color and variant props.

examples.name: Title
examples.code: <Alert title="Your current access level limits what you can view or modify" />
examples.details: You can optionally include a title for your alert with the title prop (or the title slot).

examples.name: Description
examples.code:
<Alert>
  <template #description>
    We're working on centralizing SCIM and invite settings. For now, setup is handled within individual product settings. <TextLink href="#">Learn more</TextLink>
  </template>
</Alert>
examples.details: You can optionally include description text for your alert with the description prop, or the description slot for rich content.

examples.name: Actions
examples.details: You can add actions to the alert with the actions slot. Combine with @dismiss to add a dismiss button.

examples.name: Action placement
examples.code:
<Alert
  title="Our terms of service has been updated"
  description="We've updated our terms to clarify how we handle data, billing, and user permissions. Please review and accept the latest terms to avoid impacting your service."
  actions-placement="bottom"
>
  <template #actions>
    <Button color="primary" variant="soft" pill>Set reminder</Button>
    <Button color="primary" variant="solid" pill>Review terms</Button>
  </template>
</Alert>
examples.details: Actions are automatically positioned in the alert by default. You can force a specific position with the actions-placement prop by passing either 'end' or 'bottom'.

examples.name: Indicator
examples.details: Alert provides an indicator icon by default. You can override it with the indicator slot, or pass :indicator="false" to hide it entirely.

examples.name: Dismissible
examples.details: The suggested approach for dismissible notices is to use labeled buttons in the actions slot. You can also listen to @dismiss to render a dismiss button in the alert chrome.

examples.name: Banner
examples.details: Use banner for a full-width strip across the top or bottom of a page or panel: offline, read-only, a new version. It drops the rounded corners and keeps only the lines above and below. Pass :indicator="false" for a plain strip.

components.name: Avatar
components.description: An avatar for user identities that shows an initial, a photo or an icon, with overflow counts, semantic colors and roundness options.

props.name: name
props.description: Display name; used for text initial when no image/icon

props.name: Icon
props.description: Icon component for icon avatar, bound as :Icon

examples.name: Overview
examples.details: A variety of avatar types: text, image, icon, and overflow.

examples.name: Text
examples.code: <Avatar name="David" :size="48" />
examples.details: For text-based avatars, a single initial is displayed based on the name prop passed to the component.

examples.name: Image
examples.code:
<Avatar
  name="Tyler"
  image-url="https://gravatar.com/avatar/9531b260b9693f3394bea8646c6ea141ce58fe5a138b7db7729d60a4c5dde552"
  :size="48"
/>
examples.details: To display an image avatar, provide an absolute URL to the image with image-url. Images will have a soft fade entrance once loaded, or fall back to a text display if the image fails to load.

examples.name: Icon
examples.code:
<Avatar
  :Icon="Robot"
  :size="48"
/>
examples.details: To display an icon avatar, pass an icon component to the Icon prop, for example Robot imported from @plexui/vue/components/Icon. The name prop is not used in this case, and can be omitted.

examples.name: Overflow count
examples.code: <Avatar :overflow-count="overflowCount" :size="size" />
examples.details: To display an overflow avatar, provide a number to the overflow-count prop. The number will be automatically formatted and scaled to fit.

examples.name: Sizing
examples.code: <Avatar name="David" :size="size" />
examples.details: To size the avatar, pass a number to the size prop, which will set the width and height in pixels. Text and icon avatars will scale their sizes dynamically based on this value.

examples.name: Colors & variants
examples.code: {{ variant }}
examples.details: You can stylize the display of the avatar using the color and variant props.

examples.name: Roundness
examples.code:
<Avatar
  name="Acme, co."
  color="primary"
  variant="solid"
  :size="size"
  :class="'rounded-' + roundness"
/>
examples.details: By default, avatars are fully rounded. You can override this by passing a Tailwind rounding class to class.

examples.name: Interactive
examples.details: Avatars can be used as interactive elements by listening to @click (or @pointerdown). The avatar then renders a button and applies semantic and visual interaction styles.

components.name: Avatar Group
components.description: Stacks user avatars into a single overlapping cluster, with a configurable stacking direction and one size for the whole group.

props.name: size
props.description: Size of all avatars in the group

props.name: class
props.description: Applied to the group container; other attributes are not forwarded

examples.name: Overview
examples.code:
<AvatarGroup :size="42">
  <Avatar name="Tyler" image-url="https://gravatar.com/avatar/9531b260b9693f3394bea8646c6ea141ce58fe5a138b7db7729d60a4c5dde552" />
  <Avatar name="Jane" color="primary" variant="solid" />
  <Avatar name="Tech support" :Icon="Robot" variant="solid" />
  <Avatar :overflow-count="5" />
</AvatarGroup>

examples.name: Stacking direction
examples.code:
<AvatarGroup :stack="stack" :size="42">
  <Avatar name="Tyler" image-url="https://gravatar.com/avatar/9531b260b9693f3394bea8646c6ea141ce58fe5a138b7db7729d60a4c5dde552" />
  <Avatar name="Will" />
  <Avatar name="Tech support" :Icon="Robot" variant="solid" />
  <Avatar :overflow-count="5" variant="soft" />
</AvatarGroup>
examples.details: You can control the stacking direction using the stack prop, as either "start" or "end".

examples.name: Group sizing
examples.code:
<AvatarGroup :size="size">
  <Avatar name="Tyler" color="info" />
  <Avatar name="Jane" color="discovery" />
  <Avatar name="Will" color="danger" />
  <Avatar :overflow-count="5" />
</AvatarGroup>
examples.details: You can control the size of all avatars in the group by passing size directly to the <AvatarGroup> component.

components.name: Badge
components.description: Compact label for statuses and inline metadata, with semantic colors, three variants and sizes, icon support, and a loading state.

examples.name: Overview
examples.code: Successful In progress Failed Beta Caution
examples.details: Status badges in different colors and compositions.

examples.name: Colors & variants
examples.code: {{ color }}
examples.details: You can stylize the display of the badge using the color and variant props.

examples.name: Size & roundness
examples.code: <Badge color="info" :size="size" :pill="pill">New</Badge>
examples.details: You can control the size and roundness of the badge with size and pill props. When pill is set, extra horizontal gutter is dynamically applied to the badge.

examples.name: Icon
examples.code: <Badge color="warning" size="lg"><Flask /> Beta</Badge>
examples.details: Content within the badge can be composed, like showing icons. Color, sizing, and spacing adapt by default.

examples.name: Loading
examples.code:
<Badge size="lg" color="secondary" class="gap-1.5">
  <LoadingIndicator /> In progress
</Badge>
examples.details: In this example, additional gap is added with a Tailwind gap-1.5 class to provide the appropriate visual spacing.

components.name: Breadcrumb
components.description: The trail of pages that leads to the current one, above a page title, with links, plain steps and the current page.

props.name: size
props.description: Text size: sm above a compact header, md above a page title

examples.name: Overview
examples.code:
<Breadcrumb>
  <BreadcrumbItem href="#">Home</BreadcrumbItem>
  <BreadcrumbItem href="#">Settings</BreadcrumbItem>
  <BreadcrumbItem current>Members</BreadcrumbItem>
</Breadcrumb>
examples.details: Breadcrumb renders a nav landmark named "Breadcrumb" around an ordered list. An item with href or to is a link (internal paths use the link component from PlexUIProvider, such as vue-router's RouterLink); the current item is plain text marked aria-current="page".

examples.name: Sizes
examples.code:
<Breadcrumb size="sm">
  <BreadcrumbItem href="#">Projects</BreadcrumbItem>
  <BreadcrumbItem href="#">Website</BreadcrumbItem>
  <BreadcrumbItem current>Deployments</BreadcrumbItem>
</Breadcrumb>
<Breadcrumb>
  <BreadcrumbItem href="#">Projects</BreadcrumbItem>
  <BreadcrumbItem href="#">Website</BreadcrumbItem>
  <BreadcrumbItem current>Deployments</BreadcrumbItem>
</Breadcrumb>
examples.details: Use size="sm" for a trail above a compact header; the default md sits above a page title.

examples.name: Separator
examples.code:
<Breadcrumb>
  <template #separator>/</template>
  <BreadcrumbItem href="#">acme</BreadcrumbItem>
  <BreadcrumbItem href="#">design-system</BreadcrumbItem>
  <BreadcrumbItem current>README.md</BreadcrumbItem>
</Breadcrumb>
examples.details: A small chevron stands between items by default. The separator slot replaces it, such as with a slash for file paths. Separators are hidden from assistive technology.

examples.name: Long trails
examples.code: Workspace Customer accounts Northwind Traders Archived Invoice 2024-0193
examples.details: A trail that does not fit wraps onto the next line instead of leaving the screen. An item without href is a plain step; listen to @click to make it act as a button.

props.name: href
props.description: Link destination. Internal paths use the link component from PlexUIProvider

props.name: to
props.description: Router destination, for link components that take to

props.name: current
props.description: The current page: plain text marked aria-current="page"

props.name: @click
props.description: Makes an item without a destination act as a button

components.name: Button
components.description: Button with four variants (solid, soft, outline, ghost), eight semantic colors, icon slots, loading, and block layout.

props.name: size
props.description: Control height and default gutter/icon size

props.name: disabled
props.description: Visually and accessibly disabled; click is not emitted

props.name: disabled-tone
props.description: Default cursor instead of not-allowed while disabled

props.name: gutter-size
props.description: Horizontal padding size; defaults from size

props.name: icon-size
props.description: Size of icons in the slot; defaults from size

examples.name: Overview
examples.details: A showcase of Button's key styles: solid, soft, outline, ghost, and icon-only.

examples.name: Colors & variants
examples.code: {{ color }}
examples.details: You can stylize the display of the button using the color and variant props.

examples.name: Sizing & roundness
examples.code:
<Button :color="color" :variant="variant" :size="size" :pill="pill"><Mail /> Button <ArrowRight /></Button>
<Button :color="color" :variant="variant" :size="size" :pill="pill">Button <ArrowRight /></Button>
<Button :color="color" :variant="variant" :size="size" :pill="pill"><Mail /> Button</Button>
<Button :color="color" :variant="variant" :size="size" :pill="pill">Button</Button>
examples.details: Control height with size and horizontal padding with gutter-size. Use pill for fully rounded corners. size sets the button to a specific control height, and gutter-size sets the horizontal padding. Each size provides default values for gutter-size and icon-size props, as well as font-size. Each of these values can be overridden independently. When pill is set, extra horizontal gutter is dynamically applied to the button.

examples.name: Icons
examples.code:
<Button
  :color="color"
  :size="size"
  :gutter-size="gutterSize === 'auto' ? undefined : gutterSize"
  :icon-size="iconSize === 'auto' ? undefined : iconSize"
  :uniform="uniform"
  :variant="variant"
  aria-label="Add"
>
  <PlusLg />
</Button>
examples.details: Add icons to the default slot. Sizing is automatic via the icon-size prop. Default values for icon-size are provided through the size prop, but you can pass the prop directly to change the defaults. For icon-only buttons, there are two common approaches: Square: create perfect square icon buttons with the uniform prop. When uniform is passed, gutter-size is ignored. Combine with pill to make circular icons. Tighter gutters: applying a smaller gutter-size than size can create well-sized, but not exactly square, icon buttons.

examples.name: Block
examples.details: Create full-width buttons with the block prop.

examples.name: Disabled
examples.code: <Button color="primary" :disabled="disabled">Submit</Button>
examples.details: Use disabled to both visually and accessibly disable a button. Clicks do not emit click.

examples.name: Inert
examples.code: <Button color="primary" :inert="inert">Submit</Button>
examples.details: Use inert to accessibly disable a button without any visual changes. Note: For accessibility reasons, disabled is used instead of applying inert directly to the button. Visual disablement in the disabled prop is applied via [data-disabled].

examples.name: Loading
examples.code: <Button loading size="xl" pill><ArrowUp /> Click to load</Button>
examples.details: Use loading to display a loading indicator in the button, fading out the current content. Interactions are prevented during this state, because inert defaults to loading. Override it with inert, or use disabled to add visual disablement.

examples.name: Selected
examples.code:
<Popover>
  <PopoverTrigger>
    <Button color="primary" :selected="selected" :variant="variant">Click to open</Button>
  </PopoverTrigger>
  <PopoverContent min-width="auto" class="p-4 text-sm">
    Button should look selected
  </PopoverContent>
</Popover>
examples.details: Use selected to show that a button is in an open or selected state. The exact visual behavior differs across each variant. This behavior is automatically configured with components like Menu that apply [aria-expanded="true"] or [data-state="open"] attributes.

examples.name: Optical alignment
examples.code:
Default gutters
optically-align="start"
examples.details: Use optically-align with either "start" or "end" to offset the gutter of the button.

components.name: Button Group
components.description: Join buttons into a single visual unit for toolbars, steppers, split buttons and search affordances.

examples.name: Overview
examples.code:
<ButtonGroup>
  <ButtonGroup>
    <Button variant="outline" color="secondary" :size="size" uniform aria-label="Go back">
      <ArrowLeftSm />
    </Button>
  </ButtonGroup>
  <ButtonGroup>
    <Button variant="outline" color="secondary" :size="size">Pin</Button>
    <Button variant="outline" color="secondary" :size="size">Tag</Button>
  </ButtonGroup>
  <ButtonGroup>
    <Button variant="outline" color="secondary" :size="size">Bookmark</Button>
    <Button variant="outline" color="secondary" :size="size" uniform aria-label="More options">
      <DotsHorizontal />
    </Button>
  </ButtonGroup>
</ButtonGroup>

examples.name: Orientation
examples.code:
<ButtonGroup orientation="vertical" aria-label="Zoom controls">
  <Button variant="outline" color="secondary" :size="size" uniform aria-label="Zoom in">
    <PlusSm />
  </Button>
  <Button variant="outline" color="secondary" :size="size" uniform aria-label="Zoom out">
    <Minus />
  </Button>
</ButtonGroup>
examples.details: Pass orientation="vertical" to stack the buttons, useful for + / − steppers, zoom controls, or any vertical toolbar.

examples.name: Size
examples.details: Set size on every Button inside the group so corner radii match. Mix icon-only (uniform) with text buttons; each child keeps its own padding.

examples.name: Nested
examples.code:
<ButtonGroup aria-label="Pager">
  <ButtonGroup>
    <Button v-for="page in 5" :key="page" variant="outline" color="secondary" :size="size">{{ page }}</Button>
  </ButtonGroup>
  <ButtonGroup>
    <Button variant="outline" color="secondary" :size="size" uniform aria-label="Previous page">
      <ArrowLeftSm />
    </Button>
    <Button variant="outline" color="secondary" :size="size" uniform aria-label="Next page">
      <ArrowRightSm />
    </Button>
  </ButtonGroup>
</ButtonGroup>
examples.details: Place ButtonGroup inside ButtonGroup to create visually separated sub-groups. The outer group automatically adds a small gap between children; pagination with arrow navigation is the canonical pattern.

examples.name: Separator
examples.code:
<ButtonGroup>
  <Button variant="soft" color="secondary" :size="size"><Undo /> Undo</Button>
  <ButtonGroupSeparator />
  <Button variant="soft" color="secondary" :size="size">Redo <Redo /></Button>
</ButtonGroup>
examples.details: Drop a ButtonGroupSeparator between items to add a visible divider, commonly used for Undo / Redo pairs or any "two related actions" toolbar.

examples.name: Split
examples.code:
<ButtonGroup>
  <Button variant="soft" color="secondary" :size="size"><Filter /> Filter</Button>
  <ButtonGroupSeparator />
  <Button variant="soft" color="secondary" :size="size" uniform aria-label="Add filter">
    <Plus />
  </Button>
</ButtonGroup>
examples.details: The classic split button: an action joined to a secondary affordance via ButtonGroupSeparator. Useful for Save / Save-As, Filter / Add-filter, Delete / Undo.

examples.name: Input
examples.code:
<ButtonGroup>
  <Input placeholder="Search docs..." :size="size" />
  <Button variant="outline" color="secondary" :size="size" aria-label="Search">
    <SearchSm />
  </Button>
</ButtonGroup>
examples.details: Join an Input to a trailing Button for inline search, token entry, or URL shorteners. The input flexes to fill the row; the button hugs its content.

examples.name: Input group
examples.code:
<ButtonGroup style="width: 100%; max-width: 280px">
  <ButtonGroup>
    <Button variant="outline" color="secondary" pill :size="size" uniform aria-label="Add attachment">
      <Plus />
    </Button>
  </ButtonGroup>
  <ButtonGroup>
    <Input
      pill
      :size="size"
      :placeholder="voiceEnabled ? 'Recording your idea…' : 'Describe a component…'"
      :disabled="voiceEnabled"
    >
      <template #endAdornment>
        <InputAdornmentButton
          :color="voiceEnabled ? 'caution' : undefined"
          aria-label="Toggle voice mode"
          :aria-pressed="voiceEnabled"
          @click="voiceEnabled = !voiceEnabled"
        >
          <Mic />
        </InputAdornmentButton>
      </template>
    </Input>
  </ButtonGroup>
</ButtonGroup>
examples.details: Richer composition for message composers: wrap each slot (leading action, flexible Input) in its own ButtonGroup so the outer group inserts a gap between them. The voice toggle rides inside the input via the endAdornment slot. Use InputAdornmentButton: it sizes off the input's own size token so the button stays concentric with the pill at every size.

examples.name: Dropdown menu
examples.code:
<ButtonGroup>
  <Button variant="outline" color="secondary" :pill="false" :size="size">Export</Button>
  <Menu>
    <MenuTrigger>
      <Button variant="outline" color="secondary" :pill="false" :size="size" uniform aria-label="More export options">
        <ChevronDownMd />
      </Button>
    </MenuTrigger>
    <MenuContent align="end" :min-width="200">
      <MenuItem @select="() => {}"><FileImage /> PNG image</MenuItem>
      <MenuItem @select="() => {}"><FileCode /> SVG vector</MenuItem>
      <MenuItem @select="() => {}"><FileDocument /> PDF document</MenuItem>
